speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the exact nature of the pain in your back and leg, and did it start after a specific injury or movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any numbness, tingling, or weakness in the affected leg, and can you perform a straight leg raise without the pain shooting further down? I also need to know if you have any loss of bladder or bowel control.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you didn't mention any numbness, tingling, weakness, or bladder/bowel issues, which helps rule out severe nerve compression or cauda equina syndrome. Given the sudden onset during exercise and radiation to the foot, I suspect a lumbar disc herniation. REQUEST TEST: Lumbar MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Lumbar Spine Findings: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms an L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the nerve root, which aligns perfectly with your symptoms. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lumbar disc herniation
